title: The Worst Birthday
notes: Recurring detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran Mouri, Inspector Yokomizo) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed edge between the entities involved. case_type: murder. The old cases/ep589-590 file's culprit (Takehiko Kokubu) and its car-misidentification clue both check out against the transcript -- no culprit correction needed here, unlike some other rebuilds. What the old file missed: it had zero named relationships or specific motives (everything was a generic 'knows' edge to the victim), omitted the ashtray-swap trick and the shaken-soda-can trap that were central to how the locked room was actually pulled off, omitted Eri Kisaki being questioned as a suspect herself before the mechanism was found, and omitted the cigarette-butt evidence that placed Seiji in his mother's room. One transcript inconsistency: subs give Takehiko's own room as '306' early on (0589 line ~122) but the finale's ashtray-swap reveal (0590 line ~300) mislabels it '309' (the crime scene's own number) -- treated as a subtitle/OCR slip and resolved using the earlier, internally-consistent '306' for Takehiko's room, since the crime-scene ashtray (weapon) and the swapped-in replacement cannot both have ended up in the same room per the deduction's own logic.

clues.desc: Takehiko called a Porsche 911 James Dean's car, but the actor's real car was the 550 Spyder -- his wife's birthday gift, and the only one with an open seat well that could brace a bed leg.
Evenly-spaced blood dots at the bed's foot match the tire trail a rolling buffet cart left in spilled ketchup -- proof something on wheels, not a dragged bed, crossed the bloodstain.
